author: Yffe
content:
Failing tests at thermite-spec/tests/divergence_adt_validate.rs::divergence_lowercase_variant_bypasses_exhaustiveness and ::divergence_lowercase_arm_masks_unhandled_variant demonstrate the divergence.

ROOT CAUSE: parse_path_pattern (thermite-syntax/src/parser.rs) disambiguates a single-segment match-arm pattern into Pattern::Enum vs Pattern::Binding by FIRST-LETTER CASE alone ('an uppercase-initial single segment is a zero-field enum pattern', else a binding). But parse_enum places NO casing constraint on a variant DECLARATION (take_ident('a variant name')), so an enum may declare a lowercase variant. A lowercase variant named in a match arm parses as Pattern::Binding (a catch-all); variant_pattern_name returns None for it; check_match_exhaustiveness then infers no matched enum (or treats the arm as a wildcard), and a genuinely non-exhaustive match over a declared enum is ACCEPTED (Ok(())).

AUTHORITY: .design/basis/01-adts.md REQ-5 (NonExhaustiveMatch{missing}) + REQ-12 (handled-or-loud compile-time tooth — 'a non-exhaustive match does not compile'). R-DEFER-9.

CASE 1: enum E { foo, bar } ; match e { foo => 0 } -> expected NonExhaustiveMatch{missing:[bar]}, actual Ok(()).
CASE 2 (worst): enum Shape { Circle(u64), Rect{w,h}, tri } ; match s { Circle(r) => r, tri => 0 } -> Rect modeled-but-unhandled, expected NonExhaustiveMatch containing Rect, actual Ok(()).

The fix root cause lies in the parser/validator boundary (variant-name casing is not load-bearing in the design); the validator must not treat a lowercase ident matching a declared variant as a catch-all. This divergence requires the generator/fixer to resolve; the failing tests are the block.
